doc.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021

title: First big band chart in high school
summary: Sam DeAngelo wrote hip charts for the school stage band and encouraged Kirchner, whose first chart was 'A Taste of Honey'.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well as we go along we have more and more in common. I want to take you back, you mentioned Mr. DeAngelo, and can you recall the feeling or your reaction to the first time you heard one of your early arrangements played?
Oh yeah. I wrote my first big band chart for Sam when I was in high school. We had a quote stage band. And he was a piano player and an arranger and he wrote charts for the

band on things like “Comin’ Home Baby” and “So What.” I mean this was late 60s, early 70s. And I mean for the time, that was very hip for any kind of school band, college or high school. I mean this was a high school band. So the fact that he was writing charts for us was, this was so cool. So I got interested in writing and he encouraged me to write and I wrote this chart on “A Taste of Honey,” you know the Bobby Scott tune? So that was my first chart for a big band. And we played it and it wasn’t bad. I mean I didn’t know a lot about voicing for horns and stuff like that, but I knew enough to come up with something that sounded halfway decent. And it was a great thrill you know, you can imagine, you come up with something like that that’s your own, it’s a whole new part of you that you didn’t know you had and like bam, there it is.
Did any of the players in the band provide some feedback like, “I can’t play that. That’s really awkward.”
No, no, nothing. Everything seemed to lay okay. Nobody said anything to the contrary to me anyway.
